relevance_note: The paper reports four related patients carrying a TNFAIP3 variant: 'A heterozygous c.1727dupC variant in the TNFAIP3 gene (NM_006290) ... was identified in the Pt1 and her mother (Pt 4)', and 'The same frameshift mutation was also present in the two sisters, Pt2 and Pt3'.
method_note: Read the full paper by hand; a Python script in the scratch directory only assembled the cells I wrote and checked spans and fields; no table was transcribed by script. Table 1 has patients as rows (merged cells repeated per row). Individuals: Pt1-Pt4 (all carriers) plus the father, included as a tested relative (trio WES on Pt1 and her parents; his PBMCs/plasma used as a comparator). His genotype is not stated explicitly (the variant is reported only in Pt1 and her mother), so he has no variant row and all checklist items are not reported. Inheritance 'inherited maternal' for Pt1-Pt3 is read from trio testing showing the variant in Pt1 and her mother (Pt4); the paper never uses the word 'inherited'. Zygosity for Pt2/Pt3 rests on 'the same frameshift mutation' plus the pedigree legend. 'four consanguineous patients' in the abstract describes relatedness among the patients; parental consanguinity is not stated, so consanguinity = not reported. Age at onset 'Early childhood (less than 2 years)' (Table 1, all patients) is an upper bound, so no ISO duration was given. Age at HA20 diagnosis is not given for anyone. Vital status not stated explicitly (left not reported). Feature onset fields hold only ages the paper ties to onset ('presented', 'developed', 'since'); ages at which a feature was diagnosed or led to admission (Pt1 thyroiditis at 5, Pt2 diabetes at 9, Pt4 thyroiditis at 41) are in severity_or_detail. Group statement: 'Only Pt3 presented with recurrent episodes of fevers' names the group, so recurrent fever is excluded for Pt1, Pt2, Pt4 (inferred from group statement). Unnamed counts (genital ulcers in 1, thyroiditis 3/4, arthritis 2/4, pSTAT1 increase in 3 of 4) excluded no one. Pt3 'no autoimmune manifestation up to the age of 14' was used to exclude the autoimmune-specific checklist items (thyroiditis, type 1 diabetes, autoimmune hepatitis, autoimmune cytopenia) but not arthritis/arthralgia or autoantibodies. Short stature mapped to the checklist item 'growth failure'. Normal GH secretion tests recorded as excluded growth hormone deficiency. Pt4 anti-TG 77 U/ml is listed under 'Autoantibody Positivity' but is below the stated normal value (<100 U/ml); no separate anti-TG row was made for Pt4. Contradictions/discrepancies: (1) Pt3 is 'a 13 year-old girl' but Results say 'no autoimmune manifestation up to the age of 14'. (2) Height: Pt2 '3° centile' (text) vs '3°-25° centile' (Table 1); Pt3 '3° centile' vs '<3° centile'; Pt4 adult height '10-20° centile' vs 'Short stature (10-25°)'; Results say final height 'below or slightly above 3rd percentile' for all. (3) Onset: Table 1 gives early childhood (<2 years) for all, text says 'since childhood' for Pt3 and Pt4. (4) Pt1 hydroxychloroquine appears only in the functional results, not in Table 1. No genomic coordinates or ACMG codes printed; transcript printed without version (NM_006290).
